fetching_magnet_metadata: Fetching torrent details from the magnet link…
hint_watch_label: The label every torrent added from the watched folder gets.
magnet_metadata_unavailable: Could not fetch the magnet’s details; adding it anyway
hint_auth_block: How long a blocked address stays blocked, in seconds.
hint_auth_failures: How many failed logins from one address before it is blocked.
hint_auth_window: The window the failures are counted in, in seconds.
hint_keep_alive: Seconds an idle connection is held open. 0 turns keep-alive off.
hint_max_body: Largest request the server will accept, in megabytes.
hint_low_disk: Pause everything when free space on the save path drops below this percentage.
alt_speed_explain: A second pair of limits and a switch. The schedule below throws that switch; the toolbar button throws it by hand.
alt_speed_schedule: Switch to them on a schedule
incomplete_folder: Keep incomplete downloads in a separate folder
share_action_remove_data: Remove the torrent and its files
share_limits_explain: Stop seeding once a torrent has given back enough. Either limit is enough on its own, whichever comes first.
share_limits_on: Stop seeding when a limit is reached
tracker_url_invalid: That is not a tracker address. It needs a scheme (http, https, udp, ws or wss) and a host.
watch_folder: Add torrents from a watched folder
cli_set_alt_speed: use the alternative speed limits now
cli_set_incomplete_folder: download to a separate folder first
cli_set_share_limit_action: what happens when a share limit is reached
cli_set_share_limits: stop seeding when a limit is reached
cli_set_watch_folder: add torrents dropped into a folder
cli_set_watch_start: start torrents added from the folder
database_backup_key: Back the key file up together with the database, never separately: without it nobody can recover the database, including you.
database_explain: Encrypting protects your settings and torrent list if the file is copied off this machine - a backup, another account, a disk taken out of it - and any change made without the key is detected rather than silently accepted. NanoTorrent unlocks it automatically, so there is no password to type; that also means it cannot protect against software already running as you.
database_failed: The database could not be converted
database_prompt_body:
NanoTorrent keeps your settings and torrent list in a plain SQLite file that any program can read and change without NanoTorrent knowing.

Encrypting it protects that file if it is copied off this machine, and a change made outside NanoTorrent is then detected rather than silently accepted. It unlocks automatically, so there is no password to type - which also means it cannot protect against software already running as you.

You can change this later under Preferences > Database.
settings_transfer_explain: Writes the settings you have changed, plus your labels and filters, to a JSON file. The proxy password, the web interface password and the permissions you granted each plugin are left out on purpose.
transfer_failed: The settings could not be transferred
add_magnet_link_s_description: Magnet links or info hashes (one per line)
add_to_session_and_seed: Add to session and start seeding
all_files_unticked: Every file is unticked in at least one torrent.
all_torrents_already_in_session: Not adding any torrents, since they are all added already…
app_credit: A Rust port of PicoTorrent (by Viktor Elofsson), built on librqbit.
changes_applied_on_ok: Changes are applied when you press Ok.
cli_set_bind_interface: network interface to bind all traffic to, e.g. a VPN's
cli_set_strict_network: stop rather than leak: switch off what the proxy or interface cannot cover, and refuse to start without it
cli_set_proxy_password: proxy password, for the credentialed proxy types
cli_set_proxy_username: proxy username, for the credentialed proxy types
perm_data: Remember its own data between restarts
perm_read: See your torrents and transfer rates
perm_remove: Remove torrents and delete their files
perm_storage: Move downloaded files to another folder
perm_ui: Show a window of its own
plugins_none: No plugins found. Put .rhai files in the plugins folder.
plugins_security_note: Plugins run with the access you approve, which can include removing torrents, deleting their files and contacting servers on the internet. Only use scripts you trust.
show_padding_files: Show padding files in file lists
choose_folder: Choose a folder on the NanoTorrent machine
cli_applies_note: Changes apply the next time NanoTorrent starts.
cli_db_flag_status: show whether the settings database is encrypted
cli_db_flag_encrypt: encrypt it, unlocking automatically from now on
cli_db_flag_decrypt: write it back out in the clear
cli_db_flag_export: write the settings to a JSON file
cli_db_export_note: An export carries the settings you have changed, plus your labels and filters. It deliberately leaves out the proxy password, the web interface password and the permissions you granted each plugin: a plain file is the wrong home for the first two, and a settings file that could grant plugin permissions would undo the reason the database can be encrypted at all.
cli_db_writes_note: Everything except --database-status and --export-settings writes to the database, so close NanoTorrent first.
cli_db_key_windows: The key is sealed to this Windows account, so the database cannot be opened by another user or on another machine.
cli_db_key_unix: The key is stored with owner-only permissions. Copying the profile directory copies the key with it, so it guards against other accounts rather than against someone taking the whole folder.
cli_db_already_encrypted: The database is already encrypted. Nothing to do.
cli_db_encrypted: Database encrypted. It unlocks automatically from now on.
cli_db_not_encrypted: The database is not encrypted. Nothing to do.
cli_db_decrypted: Database decrypted. It is now a plain SQLite file.
cli_db_export_omits: The proxy password, the web interface password and your plugin permissions are not in this file.
cli_web_needs_password:
Web interface enabled, but no password is set - it will not listen yet.
Set one with:  nanotorrent --set-web-password
cli_password_prompt: Enter a new web interface password (it will be visible as you type):
cli_password_pipe_hint: To avoid that, pipe it instead:  echo -n 'password' | nanotorrent --set-web-password
cli_bool_note: Booleans take true or false. --list-settings adds each one's current value.
cli_flag_list_settings: show every setting and its current value
cli_forwarded_note:
Torrent files and magnet links are opened in the running
instance if there is one.
cli_plugins_flag_onoff: enable or disable the Rhai plugin host
cli_set_check_updates: check GitHub for a newer release at startup
cli_set_low_disk_limit: free space below which to pause
cli_set_show_padding_files: list BEP 47 padding files, which are alignment rather than content
cli_set_lsd: local service discovery (BEP 14), for peers on the same network
cli_set_pause_on_low_disk: pause everything when the disk runs low
cli_set_proxy_peers: send peer traffic through the proxy
cli_set_proxy_trackers: send tracker traffic through the proxy
cli_set_skip_add_dialog: add torrents without showing the dialog
cli_set_web_disconnect_timeout: time a stalled client may hold a worker
cli_set_web_enabled: run the web interface (see also --webui on|off)
cli_set_web_auth_max_failures: failed web logins from one address before it is blocked (0 disables)
cli_set_web_auth_window: seconds over which those failed logins are counted
cli_set_web_auth_block: seconds an address stays blocked once it has tripped
auth_lockout_hint: 0 failed logins disables the lockout. Counted per address, so nobody can lock you out of your own client.
cli_set_web_request_timeout: time a client may take to send its headers
cli_web_bind_address: 127.0.0.1 (default) or 0.0.0.0 to reach it from the LAN
cli_web_flag_onoff: enable or disable the web interface
cli_web_flag_password: read a new password from stdin
cli_web_password_note: Setting a password without a terminal echoing it:
cli_web_tls_off_note:
tls_mode=off is refused at startup on anything but 127.0.0.1, because Basic
auth credentials would then cross the network in clear text.
close_prompt_body:
Do you want to exit NanoTorrent?

You can keep it running in the notification area and exit later from the tray icon.
confirm_delete_files:
Also DELETE the downloaded files from disk?

Confirming deletes them; cancelling keeps them.
files_hint: pick as many as you like
give_magnet_or_file: Give a magnet link or choose a .torrent file.
give_not_both: Give magnet links or files, not both.
label: Label
name: Name
pause_on_low_disk_space: Pause when disk space is low
bind_interface_hint: e.g. wg0, or a VPN adapter name
strict_network_hint: Switches off DHT, uTP, local discovery and UPnP when the proxy or interface cannot cover them, and refuses to start if the interface is missing.
remove_keeps_files: Removing keeps the downloaded files on disk. Removing with data deletes them permanently.
set_default_associations: Set as default for .torrent files && magnet links
some_torrents_already_in_session: Skipping the torrents that are already added…
web_advanced_hint: Timeouts are in seconds. Values outside the supported range are clamped when saved. Changes apply when the interface restarts.
web_needs_cert: Choose a certificate and a private key for the custom TLS mode.
web_needs_password: Set a password: the web interface will not start without one.
web_needs_tls: TLS cannot be off when listening on a non-loopback address - the password would be sent in clear text.
